newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Suzano drops out of CVRD bidding-paper.
newsitem.headline: Suzano drops out of CVRD bidding-paper.

text.p: Brazil's Cia Suzano de Papel e Celulose has become the second firm in two days to drop out of the planned bidding on state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce, financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said.
The paper said Suzano left a consortium led by local Cia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN)steel firm over a disagreement regarding the terms of its financial participation in the group.

Gazeta, which did not cite its source, said CSN President Benjamin Steinbruch spent much of Tuesday meeting with Suzano chief Max Feffer but the two failed to reach an accord to keep the paper firm in the group.
Suzano's exit came 24 hours after aluminum company Alcoa announced it was leaving the CSN-led group, also after failing to reach an agreement on its financial participation in the consortium.
Remaining members of the Valepar group include Gencor, Nations Bank, Opportunity Asset Management and four local pension funds.
Gazeta said the Nations Bank, which was at first only going to finance Suzano's participation in the group, now will take part directly in the consortium.
CSN is slated to square off today against a consortium led by Brazil's paper, steel and cement concern Votorantim when the government tries again today to privatize the mining conglomerate.

An auction slated for Tuesday morning at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange was thwarted by a flood of court injunctions suspending the sale. A new auction was set for 1000 local/0900 EDT Wednesday at the bolsa.
